claims.explanation: Mitoxantrone kills cells by poisoning TOP2A and trapping cleavage complexes, so selectivity is dominated by drug efflux and DNA-damage/apoptotic competence rather than by a single oncogenic driver. High ABCG2 (BCRP) efflux is the best-established resistance mechanism, while intact p53/CD95 apoptotic signaling and high TOP2A expression sensitize cells.

features.basis: BCRP/ABCG2 overexpression confers mitoxantrone resistance via ATP-dependent efflux
mitoxantrone is a topoisomerase II poison; target abundance increases cleavage-complex formation
p53 is required for CD95 receptor upregulation and apoptosis after mitoxantrone DNA damage
p53-dependent CD95/Fas induction mediates drug-induced apoptosis
side-population cells co-expressing ABCG2/ABCA3 efflux mitoxantrone and survive better
multidrug-resistance efflux transporters reduce intracellular anthracenedione accumulation
MRP-family efflux can contribute to multidrug resistance phenotype
type IIA topoisomerases including Top2beta are targets of mitoxantrone
virtual-cell response shows USP1 downregulation, linking deubiquitinase-mediated DNA repair to survival
reproducibly downregulated in virtual-cell response, implicating ubiquitin-pathway dependence
reproducibly downregulated in virtual-cell response, suggesting ion-transport dependence
reproducibly downregulated in virtual-cell response, suggesting vesicle-trafficking dependence
